body:
The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> issue; enhancement; support for tapered tooling like ball mills, roundover bits and similar, router style tooling.

Part of #3351. Refs #3351. Sub-issue 8 of the plan in #3351.

Depends on #3370
Depends on #3371
Depends on #3372

## What to do

The tapered ball nose is the 3D carving tool that the maintainer named ("tapered tooling like ball mills").

1. The 3D Finish path today is a sphere support scan (`tool_law.rs`, `BALL`; `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/`). Add a drop-cutter for the union of convex atoms of the meridian: the height of the tool at a point is the HIGHEST contact height of all its atoms against the vertex, edge and facet of each triangle. Use the contact cases of the published drop-cutter for general cutters: Yau, Chuang and Lee, Int. J. Production Research 42(13), 2004, pp. 2573-2598; Hwang and Chang, Computer-Aided Design 30(8), 1998, pp. 641-647. Copy no code.
2. Atom cases: the torus zone (the ball tip, a ball when the flat is 0), the frustum (the tapered flank) and the cylinder bands. A sphere tip must give the same heights as the scan of today (pinned).
3. The step-over and scallop laws read the tip radius `corner_r` of the tapered ball, not `diameter / 2`.
4. The 3D Finish door (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:1184`) admits a `Taper` with tip form `Ball`. A sharp or flat-tip `Taper` and a `FormMill` stay refused by name. The multi-axis family keeps the `BallNose` door.

## Rules

- `effort:max`: a new toolpath algorithm (safety floor).
- The `BallNose` toolpaths and goldens do not change (pinned).

## Done means

- A tapered ball nose finishes a steep-wall fixture: the flank clears the wall, the result verifies clean, and the deviation is within tolerance (pinned, with a golden).
- On a shallow fixture, the drop-cutter of a ball gives the same heights as the support scan within 1e-9 mm (pinned).
- A fuzz test with degenerate triangles gives an error or a valid height, never a panic.
